subject: NimbusDocs — post-demo streaming SLO evaluation & next steps
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@nimbusdocs.com>, Derek Shaw <derek.shaw@nimbusdocs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: NimbusDocs — post-demo streaming SLO evaluation & next steps

Thanks again for the time this morning — great to see the live demo and the streaming use case in action. I pulled together a concise SLO evaluation matrix (attached) and a proposed set of next actions so we can convert the demo into a pilot. High level notes below.

Quick recap (what we heard)
- Primary workload: document ingestion + real-time extract + user-facing reading pane (continuous streaming of generated summaries).
- Expected peak concurrency: 300–600 concurrent sessions during business hours (burst to ~1k for scheduled crawls).
- Typical generation length per session: 150–400 tokens (median ~220).
- Streaming requirement: sub-200ms chunk delivery for interactive feel; total generation completion acceptable up to 2.0s for median requests.

SLOs we propose to validate in pilot (please confirm priorities)
- P95 end-to-end latency (first chunk) ≤ 220 ms for <= 256 token summaries (us-west).
- P99 ≤ 600 ms for median-sized streams (adaptive chunking).
- Sustained throughput target: 1.2M tokens/min across the cluster during peak.
- Concurrency target: support 600 active streaming sessions with <5% tail-loss.

Attachments included: SLO evaluation matrix (breaks down P50/P95/P99 by token bands), KV-prefix sample for cache warmup testing, and a draft pricing for Redwood Dedicated pilot.

Proposed MAP (mutual action plan) — 6 week cadence
1) Pilot scoping doc + success criteria (owner: Nimbus — Elena) — due 2028-08-10
2) Environment & infra checklist (owner: Redwood — Karthik) — due 2028-08-14
3) Load test plan & scripts (owner: Redwood — Ben) — due 2028-08-17
4) Pilot run (2 weeks) and shared dashboards (owner: Nimbus + Redwood) — target 2028-08-21 to 2028-09-04
5) Post-pilot decision (accept, optimize, or escalate) — target 2028-09-06

Asks for you now:
- Please confirm the priority SLOs (first-chunk latency vs total completion) and any hard regulatory constraints on data residency.
- Can you share a sample of typical session token-length distribution (csv) so we can tweak batching/quant profiles?
- Would you be open to Redwood running an internal synthetic load test in advance of the pilot to validate infra assumptions?

I added Ben and Karthik — Ben will own load-test scripts and memory/KV cache tuning; Karthik will scope infra and get you the dedicated sizing recommendation. Monica will coordinate billing/contract questions in parallel.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for a 30-min MAP alignment next week once we hear back on priorities.

--
Irene Choi

Subject: Re: NimbusDocs — post-demo streaming SLO evaluation & next steps

Thanks Irene — really helpful summary and the matrix looks good at a glance. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Priority SLOs: first-chunk latency is our top UX constraint (users must see the first chunk within ~250ms). Total completion time can stretch to ~2.5s for complex docs.
2) Concurrency: our conservative engineer estimate is 450 active sessions with spikes to ~900 for big nightly jobs.
3) Data residency: production must run in us-west for compliance; pilot can use a shared account.

We'll send the token-length distribution CSV by EOD Monday (Derek will attach).

Two quick asks back:
- Can Redwood articulate what "<5% tail-loss" means operationally? Is that token-drop / failed stream / degraded chunking?
- Will you require us to provision a dedicated VPC for the pilot or can we start on Redwood hosted with a dedicated pool?

Elena

Elena — quick answers inline: 

> Can Redwood articulate what "<5% tail-loss" means operationally?
We define tail-loss as sessions that see an observable degradation in streaming quality (missing chunks, >2x expected token latency, or aborted streams). For the pilot we'll instrument at the token and session level and report two KPIs: token-drop-rate and session-abort-rate. Our acceptance threshold for the pilot is token-drop-rate <0.5% and session-abort-rate <1.0%, with tail latency P99 uplift not exceeding 2x baseline.

> Will you require us to provision a dedicated VPC for the pilot or can we start on Redwood hosted with a dedicated pool?
Short answer: hosted dedicated pool should be fine for initial pilot (we can reserve capacity in us-west and provide isolation guarantees). If Nimbus needs private networking or strict compliance, we can move to Private deployment in a subsequent phase. I'll include a short note about the isolation SLA in the infra checklist.

I'll start building the load-test plan and a small synthetic profile that mirrors your token distribution once Derek shares it.

Ben

Thanks — attached is the token-length distribution (nimbus_token_dist_aug.csv) and a short sample of our KV prefixes for a subset of documents. A couple of product notes: 
- We rely on prefix caching for ~65% of user reads (warm paths). If the pilot can show cache hit uplift during warmup we'd be very happy.
- For streaming chunking we usually work in 64-token chunks for the UI; first chunk tends to be 48–64 tokens.

I'll coordinate with Elena on the MAP scoping doc.

Appreciate the token distribution, Derek. A couple of operational notes from infra sizing: 
- For the 600-concurrency baseline with 220-token median and streaming at 64-token chunks, we expect the recommended Dedicated pool to be 6x A100-equivalent instances (we'll provide exact GPU-type recommendations in the infra checklist).
- We'll enable KV-prefix warmup and a small persistent cache in front of the runtime — that should get hit-rates into the 60–75% range for your described warm paths.
- Load testing plan: Redwood will run an internal synthetic test to validate latency bands, then we'll run a joint test from a Nimbus staging tenant; we'll capture P50/P95/P99 for first-chunk and completion, token-drop and session-abort.

Next actions I will own: infra checklist and sizing + dedicated pool pricing addendum (deliverable 2028-08-14). Ben will share the load-test scripts and run the initial synthetic. Irene — can you send a calendar invite for the MAP alignment meeting (30 min) for next Tuesday?

Perfect — thanks for the fast turnaround, Derek. Calendar invite sent for MAP alignment: 2028-08-08 10:00–10:30 PT. Agenda attached in the invite.

A couple of clarifying checks before the meeting:
- Pilot acceptance: we will use the SLO evaluation matrix (attached) and the following pass/fail thresholds for go/no-go: first-chunk P95 ≤ 250ms, session-abort-rate <1.0%, token-drop-rate <0.5%, and P99 completion ≤ 800ms for median docs. Are we aligned?
- If pilot meets these thresholds, Redwood will propose a Dedicated contract (6 node equivalent) with a 3-month pilot commitment and a preferential price in the attached pricing PDF.
- If we miss only latency but meet token-drop and abort thresholds, we will iterate tuning (batching, quant profiles) for two weeks and run a second validation test before deciding.

Please reply with any disagreements; otherwise we will treat these as the working acceptance criteria for the pilot. Looking forward to the alignment call.
